frameworks.name: Raw Claude Code (no framework)
frameworks.bestFor: Small, well-understood tasks and quick MVPs steered directly via plan mode and a tight CLAUDE.md.
pros: Zero setup, no methodology overhead — start immediately.
Plan mode gives read-only analysis + persisted plans that survive restarts.
A good <200-line CLAUDE.md already injects context every session.
cons: Unguided success rate is low; quality hinges on the operator's prompting.
Context rot is the main failure mode on long sessions with no phase boundaries.
No enforced spec/TDD/review discipline — rigor must be supplied manually.

frameworks.name: BMAD-METHOD
frameworks.bestFor: Large, complex builds needing a full simulated agile team (PM, Architect, Dev, UX) and heavy upfront planning/architecture.
pros: 12+ role agents covering brainstorming → deployment, collaborating in one session.
Opinionated agile flow grounded in PRD + architecture artifacts before code.
Free/open source, multi-tool, with native Claude Code skills.
cons: Heavyweight: multi-agent ceremony is overkill for small or solo work.
Steep learning curve for roles and document flow.
Rapidly evolving — churn between versions.

frameworks.name: GitHub Spec Kit
frameworks.bestFor: Greenfield features where an explicit, reviewable spec should drive a clean requirements → plan → tasks → implement pipeline.
pros: Official GitHub toolkit with a clear staged workflow + slash commands.
Agent-agnostic: Claude Code, Copilot, Gemini CLI from the same specs.
Spec stays the source of truth and drives implementation.
cons: Process discipline adds friction for trivial or exploratory work.
Greenfield-oriented; weaker brownfield delta tracking than OpenSpec.
Still requires good requirements thinking — structure isn't a substitute.

frameworks.name: OpenSpec
frameworks.bestFor: Brownfield iteration and regulated/audited work where every change is proposed, reviewed, and documented before code.
pros: Strict proposal → apply → archive state machine makes changes predictable.
First-class brownfield deltas (ADDED/MODIFIED/REMOVED) against existing behaviour.
Strong change-accountability and documentation trail.
cons: Proposal-first ceremony is heavy for quick changes.
Optimised for accountability over living-spec sync.
Smaller ecosystem than spec-kit or BMAD.

frameworks.name: Kiro (AWS agentic IDE)
frameworks.bestFor: AWS-native teams wanting spec-driven development baked into a full IDE with EARS requirements and automated hooks.
pros: Generates a three-document spec system (requirements/design/tasks) from a prompt.
Automated agent hooks and deep AWS integration.
Full IDE experience; structured requirements are first-class.
cons: AWS-centric design brings vendor lock-in.
Separate IDE, not a drop-in for an existing Claude Code workflow.
Heavier than lightweight markdown-only frameworks.

frameworks.name: Superpowers (obra / Anthropic marketplace)
frameworks.bestFor: Enforced engineering discipline — red-green-refactor TDD, systematic debugging, and fresh-agent code review — on production code.
pros: Skills enforce discipline: tests fail first, root-cause debugging, brainstorm before code.
Subagent flow: brainstorm → worktree → plan → TDD → fresh-agent review → finish.
In the official Anthropic plugin marketplace; runs across Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot.
cons: TDD-first + review gates add overhead for throwaway prototypes.
Discipline-as-text still depends on the agent following the skills.
Per-task execution rigor more than high-level product/architecture specs.

frameworks.name: GSD (Get Shit Done) for Claude Code
frameworks.bestFor: Solo devs and small teams wanting lightweight phase discipline (discuss → plan → execute → verify) without BMAD ceremony.
pros: Phase-based context engineering fights context rot, each phase in a focused context.
Built from standard Claude Code primitives (markdown skills, sub-agents, small CLI + hooks).
Spec-driven but lightweight; verifies small units in clean contexts.
cons: Fragmented ecosystem with competing forks.
Less heavyweight role modelling than BMAD.
Markdown/CLI machinery still adds learning overhead vs raw plan mode.

frameworks.name: Taskmaster (claude-task-master)
frameworks.bestFor: Turning a detailed PRD into a dependency-ordered task graph the agent works one bite-sized task at a time.
pros: Parses a PRD into structured, dependency-aware tasks; answers 'what's next?'.
Editor-agnostic MCP server — drops into Cursor, Windsurf, Claude Code, others.
Selective tool loading to cap context cost; sequencing reduces agent errors.
cons: Quality is bounded by PRD quality.
Default tool set is a notable context hit unless trimmed.
Task-management only; no TDD/review/architecture discipline of its own.

frameworks.name: Agent OS (Builder Methods)
frameworks.bestFor: Teams enforcing consistent codebase standards/conventions across many projects, injected into specs on demand.
pros: Moves conventions out of ad-hoc prompts into reusable, indexed standards.
Can extract existing patterns from a codebase into documented standards.
Tool- and language-agnostic.
cons: Standards + spec shaping, not full lifecycle orchestration or execution.
Value compounds across a team/many projects; little payoff for one throwaway repo.
Upfront investment to build the standards library.

frameworks.name: Claude Flow / Ruflo (multi-agent orchestration)
frameworks.bestFor: Large-scale parallel/autonomous workloads where swarms of agents with shared memory drain a backlog.
pros: Widely adopted multi-agent platform; coordinates swarms with shared memory.
Heavy infra: vector memory, many MCP tools; reports strong SWE-bench + cost savings.
Enterprise-grade, aimed at autonomous parallel sprints.
cons: Heavyweight and complex — overkill for small/solo projects.
Renamed (Claude Flow → Ruflo); CLI/npm names lag, causing confusion.
Orchestration-first, not a spec/PRD discipline layer; benchmarks self-reported.

frameworks.name: Aider Conventions (CONVENTIONS.md)
frameworks.bestFor: Terminal-first pair programming where one CONVENTIONS.md enforces style across any LLM, with atomic git commits.
pros: Dead-simple, model-agnostic: one markdown file forwarded to any LLM, cached for reuse.
Lives in Aider's terminal loop with automatic atomic git commits per edit.
Community conventions repo of ready-made files.
cons: Conventions layer only — no phases, specs, task graph, TDD, or orchestration.
Tied to the Aider tool rather than Claude Code's skill/agent system.
Manual curation; effectiveness scales with how well you write conventions.

guidance: Large multi-service build with heavy upfront PRD + architecture and a simulated team → BMAD-METHOD (or Kiro if AWS-native).
Solo MVP / quick well-scoped task, steer directly and ship fast → raw Claude Code (plan mode + tight CLAUDE.md), or Aider conventions for terminal pairing.
Need enforced TDD + fresh-agent code review on production code → Superpowers.
Lightweight phase discipline (discuss/plan/execute/verify) to fight context rot without ceremony → GSD; pair with Taskmaster if you already have a detailed PRD to decompose.
Greenfield feature driven by an explicit reviewable spec → GitHub Spec Kit; brownfield/regulated change needing a proposal + audit trail → OpenSpec.
Many projects/a team needing consistent reusable standards → Agent OS; large autonomous parallel/backlog-draining swarms → Claude Flow/Ruflo.
